objective: Test one bounded change: replace GACR-v4 hard residual application with a target-free continuous multiplier while freezing both the v3 residual and v4 gate.

single_changed_factor.name: target_free_continuous_residual_multiplier
single_changed_factor.definition: For gate probability p and domain-shared alpha, apply multiplier alpha + (1-alpha)*p to every candidate residual instead of a hard apply/skip action.
single_changed_factor.selection_scope: One alpha per development domain, shared across the three frozen residual/gate seeds.
single_changed_factor.identity_control: Alpha 1 produces multiplier 1 for every user and must exactly reproduce frozen GACR-v3.
single_changed_factor.frozen_components: GRAM checkpoints, candidate construction, six residual features, all v3 residual checkpoints, eight gate features, all v4 gate checkpoints, fit/calibration split and all model parameters.

alpha_selection.eligible: In every seed calibration cell: overall Recall@10, overall Recall@50, tail NDCG@10 and tail Recall@50 do not decrease versus GRAM, and broad harm is <=1%.
alpha_selection.objective: A non-identity alpha must be eligible and strictly exceed alpha 1 mean overall NDCG@10 within its domain.
alpha_selection.tie_break: Higher mean tail NDCG@10, higher mean overall Recall@50, lower maximum broad harm, then larger alpha.
alpha_selection.fail_closed: Select alpha 1 whenever no safe non-identity candidate strictly exceeds it.

decision_rule.keep_v5: V5 strictly exceeds v3 mean NDCG@10 in Toys and the six-cell macro average; Beauty is not below v3; Toys tail NDCG@10, overall Recall@50 and tail Recall@50 are not below v3; Toys mean overall Recall@50 is not below GRAM; every cell has Recall@10 nondecrease versus GRAM and broad harm <=1%; all integrity gates pass.
decision_rule.return_to_v3: Otherwise retain frozen GACR-v3 and stop the gate/soft-weighting factor.

post_run_policy: Write results only. Do not analyze, retry, read Sports/test, or start another experiment until explicitly requested by the researcher.
